notes.summary: For the chordal Fubini–Study form κ and the stipulated zero-lower-mass factor, the actual Green integral proves A and F: canonical exact pullback solutions of mass NV0, sector uniqueness, and bounded/continuous sector criteria. Area-one normalization alone does not identify κ.
notes.detailedSummary: The unchanged operator gives dd^c_xG=δ_y−κ_FS and ∫Gκ_FS=0. The actual integral Qμ is a canonical, possibly unbounded κ_FS-psh function with mean zero for every probability. For nonpolar μ, its normalized pullback solves the exact non-pluripolar equation with coefficient c=NV0/M and finite mass NV0. Continuous Qμ gives bounded continuous solutions and implies nonpolar μ. Product non-pluripolarity, nonclosedness and zero lower mass are verified directly. Exact pullback-sector uniqueness and the bounded/continuous equivalences follow from the curve current’s total mass one. Maximality of c is deferred to n3.
notes.text:
These are unverified mathematical drafts. Throughout, dd^c=i/(2π)∂bar∂ and products include the stipulated smooth-background corrections.

Fix κ=κ_FS=dd^c log(1+|z|²). Its affine density is dxdy/[π(1+|z|²)²], of area one. For finite y,
G(z,y)=log|z−y|²−log(1+|z|²)−log(1+|y|²)+1.
Since Δlog|z|²=4πδ0, our operator gives dd^c log|z|²=δ0. Thus dd^c_xG(x,y)=δ_y−κ_FS, also at infinity by changing charts. Rotation invariance reduces its mean to y=0. Under κ_FS, t=|z|²/(1+|z|²)=d_chord(z,0)² is uniform on [0,1], so ∫G(x,y)κ_FS(x)=∫_0^1(log t+1)dt=0.

Put K=1−G=−log d_chord²≥0. Uniformly in y, ∫K(x,y)κ_FS(x)=1 and ∫|G(x,y)|κ_FS(x)≤2. For any Borel probability μ, the actual integral Q(x)=∫G(x,y)dμ(y) is therefore defined in [−∞,1], belongs to L1(κ_FS), and has mean zero by Tonelli and Fubini. It is not identically −∞. Fatou applied to K proves upper semicontinuity. On a disk with κ_FS=dd^cρ, each G(·,y)+ρ is genuinely subharmonic, with a common local upper bound. Integrating the submean inequalities proves the actual Q+ρ is subharmonic. Thus Q is the canonical κ_FS-psh representative, including its actual pole values. Testing distributions and using the uniform L1 estimate gives dd^cQ=μ−κ_FS.

If Q is finite continuous everywhere, it is bounded by compactness. Locally Q+ρ is bounded subharmonic. After rescaling into [0,1], its Laplacian is dominated by local Bedford–Taylor capacity. Polar Borel sets have capacity zero, so μ charges none. The indispensable primary capacity results were freshly read in Bedford–Taylor, A new capacity for plurisubharmonic functions, Acta Math.149 (1982), Theorems 2.1, 3.5 and 6.9: https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~ebedford/PapersForM655/BTNewCapacity.pdf . Their positive change of dd^c normalization does not change zero-capacity sets or locality.

For any nonpolar μ, ν=M(h0^m/V0)⊗μ is non-pluripolar. Cover a locally pluripolar Borel set by countably many product coordinate boxes where it lies in {ψ=−∞}, with ψ nontrivial psh. Local L1 integrability and Fubini imply that for smooth-volume-almost every base point, ψ restricted to the curve is a nontrivial subharmonic function. That section of the set is polar and has μ mass zero. The exceptional base section has zero h0^m mass. Tonelli and the countable cover prove the assertion independently of the equation.

For every bounded genuine curve potential p, expansion and bounded Bedford–Taylor convergence give
MA_H(p∘π1)=N h0^m⊗(κ_FS+dd^cp).
Indeed, two curve factors vanish and m+1 base factors vanish; the surviving term has binomial coefficient N. This argument uses local smooth approximation after adding a curve potential for κ_FS. It does not require h0 to be closed.

For arbitrary genuine p, use p_j=max(p,−j). On {p>−j}, plurifine locality identifies the bounded curve current with κ_FS+dd^cp. Restrict the bounded product identity to these sets and increase j, exactly as in the supplied non-pluripolar operator. If p=Q and μ is nonpolar, {Q=−∞} is polar and μ-null. Consequently
MA_ext,H(Q∘π1)=N h0^m⊗μ=cν,
where c=NV0/M.
This computes an exact product and its mass; it does not infer equality from an attained inequality or invoke a global product theorem requiring BMP.

Since Q is genuine, nontrivial and upper bounded on a compact space, S=sup Q is finite. Therefore u=(Q−S)∘π1 is genuine H-psh, has supremum zero, solves MA_ext,H(u)=cν, and has actual finite mass NV0. Under continuous Q it is bounded continuous. In particular it supplies every coefficient 0<a≤c. The assertion that c is maximal among all potentials requires the separate proof in n3.

The product X is connected compact, H is positive Hermitian, and V0>0. It is genuinely big with strict potential 0. If h0 were closed, Stokes and bounded Bedford–Taylor approximation would give ∫(h0+dd^cv)^m=V0 for every bounded h0-psh v, contradicting v_−(h0)=0. Thus dh0≠0, and restriction to a fixed curve-point section shows dH≠0. Choose bounded h0-psh p_j with masses tending to zero, as the definition of v_− permits. The separated expansion yields
∫_X(H+dd^c(p_j∘π0))^N=N∫_X0(h0+dd^cp_j)^m→0.
Hence v_−(H)=0. No claim about v_+(H) is used.

For F sector uniqueness, let p be any genuine κ_FS-psh curve potential whose pullback solves cν. Its positive current T_p=κ_FS+dd^cp has total mass one by Stokes, and its non-pluripolar measure is at most T_p. The product identity forces that non-pluripolar measure to be μ, also of mass one. The positive difference T_p−μ has zero mass, hence T_p=μ. Therefore p−Q is a harmonic distribution and is constant on connected P1. Canonical representatives agreeing almost everywhere agree everywhere by recovery from shrinking local averages, including at common poles. Thus p=Q+C pointwise, and supremum normalization uniquely gives C=−sup Q. This proves bounded sector solution existence iff Q is bounded and continuous sector solution existence iff Q is continuous. No bounded exponential existence or stretching membership is inferred for arbitrary unbounded Q.

notes.summary: Continuous actual Qμ gives a unique bounded curve exponential solution for every λ>0, an explicit whole-family O(λ) limit, correct product normalization, and direct genuine stretching membership.
notes.detailedSummary: Uniform logarithmic tails give a compact Green operator from bounded μ-densities into C(P1). A normalized compact homotopy has fixed points exactly solving the exponential equation. Curve comparison supplies parameter-independent barriers, allowing Leray–Schauder continuation for every specified exponent and uniqueness among all bounded genuine curve solutions. With A=osc Q and B=2−min Q, the whole-family error is at most λe^A(2BA+A²/2) for 0<λ≤1. Product scalar-one normalization requires Uλ=(log c)/λ+wλ; supremum normalization changes the coefficient. All constructed bounded potentials satisfy the actual all-scale stretching definition. Critical curve subsolutions are exactly Q+C.
notes.text:
Assume the continuous actual potential hypothesis and retain κ_FS and the factor hypothesis from n1. Write q=Qμ, A=max q−min q and B=2−min q.

First prove curve comparison. For bounded genuine κ_FS-psh p,r, suppose T_p≤kT_r on E={p<r}, with 0≤k<1. Set z=max(p,r). The bounded maximum inequality gives T_z≥1_E T_r+1_Ec T_p≥T_p. Both currents have total mass one, so T_z=T_p and z−p is a nonnegative constant. A positive constant would force E=P1 and T_r=T_p, contradicting the strict ratio and mass one. Hence p≥r. The maximum inequality, including the tie-set choice, follows from locality applied to max(p,r+ε) and passage ε↓0. Distributional constant identities hold pointwise for canonical representatives.

Thus a bounded exponential subsolution l, T_l≥e^{tl}μ, lies below a bounded solution w of T_w=e^{tw}μ. Apply the ratio lemma to w and l−a on {w<l−a}, where T_w≤e^{−ta}T_l, and let a↓0. A bounded supersolution similarly lies above w. The functions
l=q−max q≤0, r=q−min q≥0,
with T_l=T_r=μ, are barriers for every t>0. Every bounded solution satisfies l≤w≤r and |w|≤A. Comparison in both directions proves uniqueness among all bounded genuine curve solutions.

For existence, K_L=min(−log d_chord²,L) is continuous on the compact curve square, including the diagonal. The continuous integrals ∫K_L(x,y)dμ(y) increase to 1−q(x). Dini gives
R_L=sup_x∫(K−K_L)(x,y)dμ(y)→0.
For |f|≤D the actual Green operator Lμf=∫G(x,y)f(y)dμ(y) differs uniformly from its continuous truncated-kernel operator by at most D R_L. Truncated-kernel images are uniformly bounded and equicontinuous. Hence Lμ maps bounded μ-densities to a relatively compact subset of C(P1), and ||Lμf||∞≤B||f||∞. These are truncations of the kernel, not densities against smooth volume.

Fix any specified λ>0. For v∈C(P1) and 0<t≤λ define
Z_t(v)=∫e^{tv}dμ, ρ_t(v)=e^{tv}/Z_t(v), R_t(v)=Lμρ_t(v),
T_t(v)=R_t(v)−t^{-1}log∫e^{tR_t(v)}dμ.
Set T_0(v)=q−∫q dμ. On bounded v-balls the densities ρ_t are uniformly bounded for 0≤t≤λ. Kernel compactness gives collective compactness of R_t and T_t. The subtracted constants lie between min R_t and max R_t. Uniform Taylor expansion at t=0 proves continuity of this compact homotopy, including its stated constant endpoint.

A fixed point v=T_t(v) has ∫e^{tv}dμ=1. Therefore Z_t(v)=1 and dd^cv=e^{tv}μ−κ_FS. It is a genuine continuous κ_FS-psh solution. Conversely every continuous solution is a fixed point, by inversion of dd^c up to constants and the mass normalization. At t=0 the unique fixed point is q−∫q dμ.

Every fixed point has norm at most A by the barriers, including the t=0 fixed point. On the open C(P1) ball of radius A+1 there are no boundary fixed points. The degree of I−T_0 is one. Compact homotopy invariance and nonzero degree give a fixed point at t=λ. The applicable primary continuation theorem was freshly retrieved in Leray–Schauder, Topologie et équations fonctionnelles (1934), pp.45–78: https://www.numdam.org/item/10.24033/asens.836.pdf . Compactness, continuity and the required a priori bounds have all been verified here. This constructs the unique bounded continuous wλ, with
κ_FS+dd^cwλ=e^{λwλ}μ, ∫e^{λwλ}dμ=1,
without a smooth-density existence premise.

The convergence is for the whole family. Write ρλ=e^{λwλ} and
wλ=q+rλ+bλ, rλ=Lμ(ρλ−1).
For 0<λ≤1 the barriers imply
||ρλ−1||∞≤λAe^A, ||rλ||∞≤BλAe^A.
From ∫e^{λwλ}dμ=1 and |e^s−1−s|≤s²e^{|s|}/2,
|∫wλdμ|≤λA²e^A/2.
Thus |bλ+∫q dμ|≤||rλ||∞+λA²e^A/2, and
||wλ−(q−∫q dμ)||∞≤Cμλ,
Cμ=e^A(2BA+A²/2).
For A=0 the solution and limit are identically zero. Subtracting suprema is 2-Lipschitz in uniform norm, giving convergence of wλ−sup wλ to q−sup q with error at most 2Cμλ.

On the product put Uλ=(log c)/λ+wλ∘π1. The exact product calculation gives
MA_H(Uλ)=N h0^m⊗e^{λwλ}μ=e^{λUλ}ν,
with actual finite mass NV0. Its supremum is Sλ=(log c)/λ+sup wλ. For Vλ=Uλ−Sλ, the correct equation is
MA_H(Vλ)=c e^{λ sup wλ}e^{λVλ}ν.
It generally is not the scalar-one equation. Vλ converges uniformly to u from n1 at the stated rate.

Every constructed bounded product potential W belongs to the task’s genuine zero-reference stretching class. It satisfies W≼0. For every real t≥1, the constant v_t=t inf_XW is genuine H-psh and satisfies t^{-1}v_t+(1−t^{-1})0≤W. This directly checks the all-scale definition; it does not assert that tW is H-psh or replace the definition by envelope equality.

For the separated critical characterization, let p be any genuine curve critical subsolution MA_ext,κ_FS(p)≥μ, initially allowing poles. Its non-pluripolar mass is at most the mass one of T_p. The inequality forces T_p=μ. The argument in n1 yields p=q+C pointwise. Conversely every such translate is critical. Thus all are ordinarily equivalent to q, and q+C≤q+D iff C≤D. The supremum-zero representative is uniquely q−sup q. Under continuous q all are bounded and pole-free. The separated product statement at coefficient c follows from the product formula. No critical uniqueness outside this sector is asserted.

notes.summary: Uλ is greatest among all genuine exponential subsolutions, including competitors with poles or infinite mass. Bounded product uniqueness and the attained unrestricted coefficient threshold c=NV0/M follow without BMP.
notes.detailedSummary: Bounded ratio domination is reconstructed from the primary Hermitian modified comparison theorem using strict positivity of H, not positive lower mass. Raising an arbitrary exponential subsolution to max(v,Uλ−k) gives a bounded subsolution and extends domination to every genuine competitor. A constant shift of any scaled subsolution is an exponential subsolution. Comparison as λ decreases to zero forces its coefficient a≤c. The exact bounded solution attains c in the unrestricted class, bounded ordinary type and genuine zero-reference stretching class. Unbounded exponential uniqueness and nonseparated critical uniqueness are not claimed.
notes.text:
Retain n1–n2. The needed comparison has no BMP or positive-lower-mass hypothesis.

The primary input is Guedj–Lu, Quasi-plurisubharmonic envelopes 2: Bounds on Monge–Ampère volumes, Algebraic Geometry9 (2022),688–713, Theorem1.5 and Lemma1.2, freshly read at https://content.algebraicgeometry.nl/2022-6/2022-6-021.pdf . A smooth positive Hermitian ω on a compact n-fold satisfies ±dd^cω≤Bω² and ±dω∧d^cω≤Bω³ for some finite positive B, by compactness. For bounded genuine ω-psh p,r, 0<τ<1, mτ=inf(p−(1−τ)r) and Eτ,s={p<(1−τ)r+mτ+s}, the modified comparison theorem gives
(1−4B(n−1)²s/τ³)^n∫_Eτ,s MA_ω((1−τ)r)≤∫_Eτ,s MA_ω(p)
for 0<s<τ³/[32B(n−1)²]. Its hypotheses require neither BMP nor smooth densities. A positive change of dd^c convention only changes B.

Reconstruct ratio domination as follows. Suppose MA_ω(p)≤kMA_ω(r) on {p<r}, 0≤k<1. Subtract a common constant so −L≤r≤0. If m=inf(p−r)<0, choose τ small with (1−τ)^n>k and τL<−m/2. Then m−τL≤mτ≤m. For sufficiently small s>0, Eτ,s is nonempty and contained in {p<r}, and D=(1−4B(n−1)²s/τ³)^n satisfies D(1−τ)^n>k. Positivity of mixed bounded products gives
MA_ω((1−τ)r)≥(1−τ)^nMA_ω(r)+τ^nω^n.
The modified comparison and assumed ratio force ∫_Eτ,s ω^n=0. A nonempty strict inequality set of genuine quasi-psh functions has positive smooth volume: upper semicontinuity controls the smaller function near a point of strict inequality, and the larger function’s local submean inequality ensures a positive-volume larger-value set. This contradiction proves p≥r everywhere. It does not establish a uniform lower mass over arbitrarily large bounds.

If bounded p satisfies MA_H(p)≥e^{λp}ν, on {Uλ<p−a} we have MA_H(Uλ)≤e^{−λa}MA_H(p). Apply ratio domination to Uλ and p−a, then let a↓0, to obtain p≤Uλ. Applying this in both directions proves uniqueness among all bounded genuine product exponential solutions.

Now allow any genuine H-psh exponential subsolution v, with additional poles or excess/infinite mass. For k>0 put v_k=max(v,Uλ−k). It is bounded genuine H-psh. The maximum inequality and locality give
MA_H(v_k)≥1_{v>Uλ−k}MA_ext,H(v)+1_{v≤Uλ−k}MA_H(Uλ−k).
For a precise tie-set justification choose j with −j<min(Uλ−k) and apply the bounded maximum inequality to max(v,−j) and Uλ−k; their maximum is v_k. Locality identifies the first branch with the original operator. On the second branch MA_H(Uλ−k)=e^{λUλ}ν≥e^{λ(Uλ−k)}ν. Hence MA_H(v_k)≥e^{λv_k}ν. Bounded comparison yields v_k≤Uλ, so v≤Uλ. This proves that Uλ is greatest among all genuine exponential subsolutions. No finite-mass assumption on v entered the argument, and genuine values at poles are preserved.

Suppose MA_ext,H(v)≥aν with a>0, and subtract sup v. For each λ>0, zλ=v+(log a)/λ is an exponential subsolution because v≤0 and e^{λzλ}=a e^{λv}≤a. Greatest-subsolution comparison gives
v≤log(c/a)/λ+wλ∘π1.
At any point where v is finite, the barriers in n2 bound wλ uniformly as λ↓0. If a>c the right side tends to −∞, a contradiction. Therefore a≤c, even for competitors with poles or infinite mass. The exact bounded solution u attains c; it has ordinary type0 and belongs to the genuine stretching class. Consequently the attainable nonnegative subsolution coefficients are exactly [0,c], and the same supremum c is attained in all three stated classes.

This is a threshold for the specified product measure, obtained without bounded-density truncation against smooth volume. It does not assert uniqueness of unbounded exponential solutions, critical-potential uniqueness outside the separated sector, or constancy of arbitrary Hermitian masses.

notes.detailedSummary: The growth hypothesis μ(B(x,r))≤Cr^δ bounds logarithmic-kernel tails uniformly by (2C/δ)e^(−δL/2), proving finite continuous actual potential. The weighted circle admits δ=1, C=2(1+ε), and explicit potential Q(re^iφ)=1−log2−log(1+s²)−εs cosφ, s=min(r,1/r). On its support Q=1−log4−ε cosφ, with range 2ε and μ mean 1−log4−ε²/2. notes.text:
Suppose μ(B_chord(x,r))≤Cr^δ for every center and 0<r≤1, with δ>0. With K=−log d_chord² and K_L=min(K,L), layer cake gives
sup_x∫(K−K_L)dμ≤∫_L^∞Ce^(−δt/2)dt=(2C/δ)e^(−δL/2).
The actual integral is finite everywhere. Each truncated-kernel integral is continuous, and the displayed uniform tail bound makes its limit continuous. Thus n1–n3 apply under the stipulated factor hypothesis. This is a direct measure criterion, not solution existence used as its own definition.

For 0<ε<1 let dμε(e^{iθ})=(1+εcosθ)dθ/(2π) on the affine unit circle. Its support is the full circle. If a ball centered anywhere meets the circle at y, its intersection lies in the circle ball centered at y of radius2r. A circle ball of radius R≤1 has normalized arc length2arcsin(R)/π≤R. Hence for r≤1/2 its weighted mass is at most2(1+ε)r; for larger r total mass one gives the same bound. Thus δ=1 and C=2(1+ε) suffice.

For z=re^{iφ}, r>0, put s=min(r,1/r). The actual potential is
Qμε(re^{iφ})=1−log2−log(1+s²)−εs cosφ,
with continuous value1−log2 at both0 and∞. To derive it expand log|re^{iφ}−e^{iθ}|² as 2log^+r−2∑_{k≥1}s^kcos(k(φ−θ))/k. The weight retains only the first cosine term. Abel regularization and the preceding uniform logarithmic tail bound justify the actual integral at r=1. On the support,
Qμε(e^{iφ})=1−log4−εcosφ.
Its range is2ε and its με mean is1−log4−ε²/2, so the potential is nonconstant on its support. The circle has smooth area zero; με is singular against smooth volume. Its product ν is concentrated on X0×S1, also of smooth volume zero, while remaining non-pluripolar by n1.

notes.text:
The combined result of n1–n4 distinguishes exact finite-mass solutions, scaled inequalities, every specified positive exponent, normalization, whole-family convergence, sector uniqueness and the unrestricted subsolution threshold. It requires the stipulated v_−(h0)=0 factor and κ=κ_FS for the given chordal distance. It uses neither BMP nor a volume-density Lp existence premise for ν.

There is an exact normalization gap if “∫κ=1” permits an arbitrary positive area-one curve form. The unchanged kernel satisfies
κ+dd^cQμ=μ+(κ−κ_FS),
not μ. Choose nonconstant smooth φ with κ=κ_FS+dd^cφ>0. For the weighted-circle measure, off its support this current is dd^cφ, which has a negative open part because it is nonzero and has integral zero. Qμ need not even be κ-psh. More simply, for μ=κ_FS the proposed Q is0, and its product has curve factorκ instead of the desiredκ_FS. Replacing Q by Q−φ would correct a different construction but changes the stipulated target. Thus A–G are proved under the standard intended identification ofκ; otherwise that missing hypothesis is a genuine gap.

The separate named-factor dependency was investigated freshly. A counterexample to positive lower Hermitian Monge–Ampère mass, https://mingchenxia.github.io/Papers/volinf0_vibe.pdf , claims the compact threefold
Y=(P3\({z=0}∪{w=0}))/⟨[z:w]↦[z:e^{2π}w]⟩
has a zero-lower-mass metric. Its proposed proof needs positive smooth dd^c-closed(2,2)-formsΓj with bounded∫h∧Γj and divergent∫Γj^(3/2), produced through trace separation and smoothing curve averages. This deliverable does not certify that complete sequence construction or import its conclusion. Its operator i/π∂bar∂ is twice the task operator, requiring potential rescaling.

Two portions can be checked independently. The quotient action is free. The function t=log(||w||²/||z||²) changes by4π under the generator. Bounded t-strips keep both projective blocks uniformly nonzero and are compact subsets ofP3; they prove proper discontinuity and compactness of a fundamental region. Thus the quotient is connected compact and complex.

For the final implication, assume the requiredΓj sequence has actually been established. A strictly positive(2,2)-form on a threefold has a unique positive square rootηj, because the cofactor map Q=2cof(H) is invertible on positive Hermitian matrices. Put Pj=∫h∧Γj and Rj=∫ηj³. Tosatti–Weinkove, Corollary1,(1.2), freshly read at https://arxiv.org/pdf/0910.1390 , applies to the smooth positive volumeηj³. With u_j=2π times its i∂bar∂ potential, it gives γj=h+dd^cuj>0, sup uj=0 and γj³=e^(bj)ηj³. Pointwise AM–GM gives γj∧ηj²≥e^(bj/3)ηj³. Since dd^cΓj=0, Stokes yields Pj=∫γj∧Γj≥e^(bj/3)Rj. Hence
∫γj³=e^(bj)Rj≤Pj³/Rj²→0.
This implication does not supply the missing independently certifiedΓj sequence.

Older primary statements of no known counterexample cannot be promoted to a current nonexistence claim, since a newer manuscript explicitly claims one. Conversely that manuscript’s claim does not replace the complete independent dependency proof required here. No concrete factor is treated as trusted. The restricted theorem remains conditional on the exact supplied factor hypothesis. Named-factor certification and original unrestricted S15’s individual criteria remain unresolved.
